issue.description:
docs/plan/plan.md section 7.1 documents delta encoding as an intended
optimization for the turns array on long matches ("for very long matches,
the turns array can use delta encoding -- only recording events that
changed from the previous turn") but this is not implemented: engine/replay.go
has no delta logic (grepped for "delta"/"Delta" in engine/replay.go --
only hit is an unrelated Direction.Delta() helper in engine/types.go).
Every turn in a replay is currently stored in full.

Each turn already only records deltas conceptually (moves, spawns,
deaths, captures, energy_collected, energy_spawned, scores -- see the
example schema in section 7.1) rather than full grid state, so the "delta
encoding" here specifically means: don't re-emit unchanged per-player
score/energy totals every turn if they didn't change since the last turn,
and consider omitting turns array entries for structurally uneventful
turns (dedupeable via the existing gzip pass, but true delta encoding
reduces pre-gzip size and, more importantly, parse/reconstruction time in
web/src/lib/replay-data.ts on load).

Concrete scope: measure current uncompressed/gzipped replay size for a
representative 500-turn 4-player match (section 7.1 estimates
200-500KB / 30-80KB), implement delta encoding for the turns array in
engine/replay.go, update the replay format version, update
web/src/lib/replay-data.ts to reconstruct full per-turn state from deltas,
and confirm the replay viewer (web/src/replay-viewer.ts) still renders
identically. Bump replay schema version and update
web/public/replay-schema-v1.json (or introduce v2) accordingly.

Value: smaller payload = faster replay-viewer first paint, especially on
mobile/slow connections, which is the primary way visitors experience
this platform (section 7.3).
issue.title: Add delta encoding for replay turns array to cut replay JSON size

issue.description:
All four ACB WorkflowTemplates failed on iad-ci on 2026-08-06, twice each
(runs ~94m and ~99m apart). Observed 2026-08-06 12:35Z.

| workflow | failing node | exit |
|---|---|---|
| acb-build-dqhxq / -fv7fs | build-api, build-worker, build-enrichment, build-evolver, build-map-evolver, build-matchmaker, build-index-builder — all 7 | 1 |
| acb-enrichment-build-lp6x4 / -swt79 | docker-build | 1 |
| acb-images-build-np4cs / -s4b8n | test | 128 |
| acb-site-pages-build-q2h78 / -sfmwc | 4 retries, "No more retries left" | 128 |

## Likely root cause: the sensor is not expanding the commit SHA

Every failed run carries its `commit-sha` parameter as the **literal
unexpanded string**:

    commit-sha = {{dependencies.acb-push.body.after}}

That is the Argo Events trigger template, not a SHA. A `git checkout` of
that literal ref fails with **exit 128**, which is exactly what
acb-images-build (`test`) and acb-site-pages-build report. The exit-1
failures in acb-build/acb-enrichment are plausibly the same checkout
failure surfacing later in the build.

`acb-build.yml` declares the parameter as `sha` with the comment "Short
commit SHA, supplied by the Argo Events sensor", while the submitted
workflows pass `commit-sha`. Worth checking whether the sensor and the
template disagree on the parameter name — that would leave `sha` unset and
`commit-sha` unexpanded, matching what we see.

## Where to look

- `declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/acb-eventsensor.yml` —
  the `acb-push` dependency and its `dataTemplate`/parameter wiring
- `declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/acb-build.yml` —
  parameter named `sha`, no default
- repo: `git.ardenone.com/jedarden/ai-code-battle`

## Reproducing

Pod logs are gone (`podGC: OnPodCompletion`). To capture them, resubmit with
a `podGC: OnWorkflowCompletion` override, or stream while running.

Note: these ran while iad-ci could not schedule new pods (see the capacity
bead in declarative-config), so confirm the failures are independent of that.
issue.notes: Root cause confirmed: each SHA src/dest mapping was placed in spec.triggers[].parameters, which parameterizes the TriggerTemplate rather than the submitted Workflow resource. That is why the original inline {{dependencies...}} value survived unchanged. Commit 1c9d10e4 replaced it with an empty value but retained the wrong parameter location; a real 2026-08-17 push then submitted acb-build-vxxgl with an empty commit-sha. Fixed in declarative-config commit 017b2e71 by moving all Forgejo ACB mappings and the parallel GitHub mapping under template.argoWorkflow.parameters, extracting body.after with dataKey, using a fail-closed sentinel, and placing conditions under the TriggerTemplate. The active acb-build WorkflowTemplate declares commit-sha; the sha argument in legacy acb-build.yml belongs to differently named templates and is not referenced by these sensors. Validation: semantic YAML assertions passed for all six mappings and referenced WorkflowTemplates; pre-commit/gitleaks passed; candidate iad-ci resource audit checked 253 files with 0 critical findings. Post-push, argo-events-ns-iad-ci is Synced/Healthy at 017b2e71, both Sensor pods are Ready, and both Sensors report DependenciesProvided/Deployed/TriggersProvided=True with only argoWorkflow-level body.after mappings. The exit-128 runs had scheduled and executed git, so the SHA failure was independent of the separate capacity issue (which could delay scheduling but cannot produce a process exit code).
issue.title: ACB CI: all four build templates failing on iad-ci; sensor passes commit-sha as an unexpanded {{...}} template (git exit 128)

the pre-flagged highlight, export it" -- directly serves the platform's

og-tags.ts) with near-zero new backend work since the data already

issue.description:
Read and analyze the focus-fire phase code in engine/turn.go to understand:
- How focus-fire targets are selected
- How damage is calculated and applied
- What conditions trigger focus-fire vs single-target combat
- The relationship between zone shrink and combat convergence

Document the current implementation with code references.

Acceptance criteria:
- Complete code walkthrough documented
- Focus-fire algorithm understood
- Edge cases identified
- Diagram of flow created if complex
issue.notes:
Focus-fire implementation walkthrough (current engine/turn.go; no source changes made).

Phase/lifecycle:
- ExecuteTurn (engine/turn.go:19-48) increments Turn, then runs Move (52-113), Combat (201-290), Zone (116-175), Capture, Collection, Spawn, EnergyTick, and Endgame in that order. Combat therefore sees post-move positions and always runs before zone deaths; it is not gated on ZoneEnabled or ZoneActive.
- MatchRunner.Run activates the zone before bot moves (engine/match.go:139-148): when !ZoneActive and (gs.Turn+1) >= ZoneStartTurn, it sets ZoneActive and calls setInitialZoneRadius. ExecuteTurn then increments the turn. If called directly without Run, ExecuteTurn does not activate the zone itself.

Combat pass 1, candidate/target selection (turn.go:201-223):
- For every living bot b, scan every bot e. Skip e if dead, e.ID == b.ID, or e.Owner == b.Owner. There is no per-player target selection, target ordering, line-of-sight, wall check, or explicit focus-fire mode.
- A candidate is any enemy satisfying Grid.InRadius(b.Position, e.Position, Config.AttackRadius2). InRadius is Distance2 <= radius2 (grid.go:113-116), and Distance2 uses the shorter toroidal row/column deltas (grid.go:78-96). Thus edge-wrap enemies can fight; walls only affect movement, not combat.
- Store the complete candidate list in botsInRadius[b.ID] and its length in enemyCounts[b.ID]. Counts are total enemy bots, not enemy players. Because the distance relation is symmetric, if b lists e, e also lists b (assuming both are alive).
- DefaultConfig uses AttackRadius2=12 (sqrt ~= 3.46), while ConfigForPlayers overrides 2-player matches to 25 (5 tiles) and 3+ players to 12 (types.go:185-203, 205-260). The value is squared Euclidean/toroidal distance, not a tile Manhattan radius.

Combat pass 2, effective damage/death rule (turn.go:225-248):
- There is no HP, damage amount, attack event, or partial damage. The only effect is binary Alive=false.
- For a bot b with n = enemyCounts[b.ID], n==0 means it survives this combat pass (234-236). Otherwise b is marked dead if any nearby enemy e has enemyCounts[e.ID] <= n (238-247). Equivalently: b survives only if it has enemies and its count is strictly lower than every nearby enemy count; ties kill both adjacent sides. This is a local strict-minimum rule, not selection of one victim.
- All counts and candidate lists are computed before any deaths are applied, so resolution is simultaneous and independent of gs.Bots iteration order for alive/dead outcomes. No newly dead bot is removed from another bot's same-turn count.
- Examples covered by tests: adjacent 1v1 gives both count 1 and mutual death (turn_test.go:93-111); 2v1 gives the lone bot count 2 and group bots count 1, so only the lone bot dies (113-133); a 3-bot formation versus one isolated bot leaves the formation alive and kills the isolated bot (135-171). A useful correction to the informal “focus fire” wording: if A has count 3 and adjacent B has count 2, A dies from comparing 3 >= 2, while that comparison alone does not kill B because B tests 2 >= 3, which is false.

Combat pass 3, application/credit (turn.go:250-290):
- For every ID in dead, mark b.Alive=false, append b to DeadBots, and decrement its owner's Player.BotCount when the owner index is valid (251-258). Combat directly performs this bookkeeping rather than calling KillBot, so it emits EventCombatDeath, not the generic EventBotDied emitted by KillBot.
- For each dead victim, killers is populated with every enemy in the precomputed botsInRadius[victim.ID], not only an enemy that caused the comparison to succeed (260-267). For each such e, increment CombatDeaths[e.Owner] if in range and add Config.KillScore to e owner's score if in range (268-275). Therefore one victim can award multiple killer credits/score increments, and a bot marked dead in the same simultaneous resolution can still receive credit for killing another victim. MatchResult carries these CombatDeaths values (types.go:263-273), which are credited to killer owners in this implementation.
- One EventCombatDeath is emitted per dead victim, with victim ID/owner/position and the full killers array (278-287). Dead bots remain in gs.Bots with Alive=false and are excluded from later phases.

What triggers focus-fire versus single-target:
- There is no branch or mode switch. Combat is triggered whenever at least one pair of opposing living bots is within AttackRadius2 after movement, including before the zone starts and even if ZoneEnabled is false. A bot with no nearby enemy is safe from combat; same-owner bots are never combat candidates.
- “Single-target” is only the degree-1 case of the same graph algorithm: in a 1v1, both counts are 1, so both die. “Focus fire” is the degree>1 case where a group’s lower per-bot enemy count beats an isolated/hotter bot. Multiple enemies do not select a target; they all become candidate killers/credits if the victim dies.
- Movement interactions: same-owner bots converging on one intended tile are killed by self-collision before combat (turn.go:88-107); opposing bots converging on the same tile move there and can fight at distance zero (if AttackRadius2 >= 0). Combat deaths do not reach the zone/capture/collection/spawn phases as living bots.

Zone shrink and convergence:
- executeZone first returns when ZoneEnabled is false (turn.go:115-119). NewGameState sets a fixed map-center ZoneCenter and an initially inactive zone (game.go:59-83). On activation, setInitialZoneRadius computes 90% of the smaller half-dimension, floors it, and enforces a minimum initial radius of 7 (turn.go:177-199).
- Once active, shrinking occurs only when Turn > ZoneStartTurn and (Turn-ZoneStartTurn) % ZoneShrinkInterval == 0 (127-140), so the start turn itself does not shrink. With ConfigForPlayers, both 2-player and 3+ matches use interval 1 and step 1; 2-player uses min radius 2 and attack radius 5, while 3+ uses min radius 1 and attack radius sqrt(12) (types.go:242-258). The unscaled DefaultConfig has min radius 1 and attack radius sqrt(12).
- After any shrink, each living bot is checked using toroidal Distance2 against the center; strictly outside radius squared is killed and gets EventZoneDeath (142-175). Zone death gives no combat kill credit/score and is separate from combat. Since combat runs first, an out-of-zone bot can participate in that turn's combat before being zone-killed; a combat-dead bot is skipped by the zone loop.
- The zone does not move bots toward the center; it only shrinks the legal circle and kills outsiders. Convergence depends on bots moving inward (they receive ZoneBounds in visible state when enabled, game.go:329-335). At the configured minima, the maximum diameter of the safe circle is <= the configured attack radius (2*2 <= 5 for two players; 2*1 <= sqrt(12) for 3+), so surviving bots in the final zone are necessarily mutually in attack range. This forces eventual contact, but arbitrary custom configs or bots that never enter the zone are not guaranteed to converge alive.

Flow diagram:
Run turn:
  zone activation (match.go:139-148)
       |
       v
  ExecuteTurn increments Turn
       |
       v
  MOVE: intended positions; invalid moves stay; same-owner destination collision -> KillBot
       |
       v
  COMBAT / focus-fire (turn.go:201-290)
    1. living bots -> all opposing bots in toroidal AttackRadius2
    2. count each candidate set
    3. mark b dead iff count(b)>0 and some neighbor count <= count(b)
    4. apply all marks simultaneously; award every listed neighbor; emit combat_death
       |
       v
  ZONE: optional shrink, then kill living bots with Distance2(center) > radius^2
       |
       v
  CAPTURE -> COLLECT -> SPAWN -> ENERGY_TICK -> ENDGAME

Important edge cases:
1. Zero nearby enemies means no combat death.
2. Equal neighboring counts cause mutual death; cycles/ties can eliminate every bot in a connected combat component.
3. Candidate lists use a snapshot, so simultaneous deaths can mutually credit one another.
4. A victim is credited to all nearby enemies, not a single selected attacker; CombatDeaths can exceed the number of victims.
5. Toroidal wrap and same-tile opponents count; walls and ownership are the only exclusions beyond Alive/self.
6. Same-owner self-collision is resolved earlier and uses a different generic death event.
7. Zone activation is external to ExecuteTurn; direct GameState callers must set ZoneActive/radius themselves. ZoneShrinkInterval <= 0 is an unsafe custom configuration because the modulo expression can panic at zero.
issue.title: Analyze focus-fire phase implementation in engine/turn.go
